name: Inspect and maintain substations
summary: Station electricians visit each of the utility's 91 municipal substations once a month to read gauges, look over transformers, breakers, batteries and the building, and fix small problems on the spot, and they carry out heavier time-based and condition-based maintenance that needs equipment switched out of service. Outage work involves the stations supervisor, a switching planner and a control room operator who issues work protection, and often a mobile substation to keep customers supplied. Routine visits are quick but compete with trouble calls and construction for the same small crew; outage work is slow because it has to be booked around summer and winter peaks, the two mobile substations and parts that can take months to arrive.

baseline.org_archetype: A city-owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers, 91 substations and a 33-person stations and protection department working days with on-call cover.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019-2022. Work orders are generated from preventive maintenance plans in the ERP and recorded on paper inspection sheets or tablets, then typed into the ERP. About half of the stations were past their expected service life.

trigger: A monthly inspection or a time- or condition-based maintenance work order falls due in the ERP and is released on the stations crew schedule.
end_state: The work is done, readings and test results are recorded in the ERP, the stations supervisor closes the work order and any findings go to asset management.

volume.seasonality: Monthly inspections are steady at about 91 a month. Outage maintenance is concentrated in April to June and September to November, between the summer air-conditioning peak and the winter heating peak, and is lighter in July, August, December and January.

evidence.note: About 91-92 stations (source says 92 in 2021) inspected monthly gives about 91 routine work orders a month; 25 to 40 outage maintenance orders a month (transformers, breakers, switchgear, batteries) is the author's estimate for a fleet of about 90 stations with roughly 180 power transformers. Agrees with the organisation file's range.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). 22 station electricians on days with on-call. Steps record elapsed crew time with people = 3 on outage work, so stated FTE covers the whole crew. The rest of their time goes to protection testing, station construction and commissioning, trouble calls and training.
Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Three supervisors; this process takes planning, outage booking and work order review.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Eight technologists; most of their time is in ops-protection-testing; here they test trip circuits and relays after breaker and switchgear maintenance.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Not listed in the process map's roles but writes the switching orders that outage maintenance needs.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Not listed in the process map's roles; issues and releases work protection from the control room.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
SCADA for stations and feeder devices
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Time entry for crews and staff
Asset condition and health index analytics
Protection settings database and relay software

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Release monthly work orders
steps.description: The ERP preventive maintenance plan generates the month's station inspection work orders and any time-based maintenance orders that fall due, and places them in the stations backlog with the station, equipment and task list attached.

evidence.note: Typical ERP plant-maintenance practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Assign work orders to electricians
steps.description: The stations supervisor reviews the backlog in the ERP against the crew calendar, vacation and trouble work, sorts routine inspections into geographic routes and flags orders that need an outage, a mobile substation or a protection technologist.

next.condition: maintenance that needs equipment out of service

evidence.note: Share of outage maintenance is the author's estimate (about 30 of 120 orders a month).

steps.name: Drive to the station
steps.description: The electrician collects the inspection sheet, station keys, gas detector and test kit, then drives a light truck to the station; a route usually takes in three or four stations in a day across urban and rural parts of the territory.

evidence.note: Visits are spread over the month around trouble calls and construction; travel time reflects a 1,116 km2 territory.

steps.name: Call the control room and log entry
steps.description: Before opening the station the electrician phones the control room operator, gives name, station and purpose, confirms no switching is planned there, and signs the station log book; the call is repeated on leaving.

control.basis: Station entry procedure in the utility's work protection code and IHSA Electrical Utility Safety Rules

evidence.note: Standard station-entry practice at Ontario distributors.

steps.name: Walk through and take readings
steps.description: The electrician walks the yard and switchgear room, records transformer winding and oil temperatures, oil levels, gas relay and pressure relief indications, tap changer and breaker operation counters, battery voltage and charger state, and checks fences, heaters, lighting, signage and for oil leaks or animal entry.

error.defect_description: A reading is misread or skipped, or a developing defect is not noticed.

next.condition: minor defect that can be fixed now

evidence.note: Equipment list from the sources; checklist content and branch shares are the author's estimate. Monthly cadence is the organisation file's estimate and common Ontario practice; not confirmed from an opened source.

steps.name: Scan equipment with an infrared camera
steps.description: On the quarterly or annual scan visit the electrician photographs bushings, connections, cable terminations and breaker cubicles with a thermal camera under load and notes any spot that is hotter than similar parts nearby.

next.condition: always; hot spots become corrective work orders

evidence.note: Infrared scanning is common station practice; interval is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draw oil samples
steps.description: For transformers due for oil testing the electrician draws oil from the sampling valve into syringes and bottles, labels them with the transformer serial number, and ships them to the testing laboratory.

error.defect_description: Sample contaminated with air or mislabelled.

evidence.note: Dissolved gas and oil quality tests are standard transformer diagnostics (source); annual sampling is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Laboratory analyses the oil
steps.description: An outside laboratory runs dissolved gas analysis and oil quality tests (moisture, acidity, dielectric strength) and emails a report that flags gas levels or trends against the IEEE limits.

evidence.note: Tests from the source; laboratory turnaround of one to three weeks is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Fix a minor defect on the spot
steps.description: The electrician replaces failed lamps, heaters or filters, tops up battery electrolyte, clears debris or nests, or repairs a fence or lock using van stock, without taking any equipment out of service.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Contain and report an oil leak
steps.description: If a transformer or breaker is leaking oil the electrician lays absorbent pads and booms, checks whether oil has left the containment, and calls the control room and the health, safety and environment advisor, who decides whether the spill must be reported to the province.

control.basis: Ontario Environmental Protection Act spill reporting (Spills Action Centre)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of practice; legal duty to report spills recalled from general knowledge.

steps.name: Plan the outage window
steps.description: The stations supervisor checks the station's load history in SCADA, the season and other planned work on the same feeders, picks a window when the load can be carried by adjacent stations or a mobile substation, and requests the outage and switching from the control centre.

evidence.note: Source says work often needs the area de-energized and may need a planned outage; timing around peaks is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the switching order
steps.description: The switching planner writes the step-by-step switching order to isolate the transformer or breaker, transfer load to other feeders or the mobile, and place grounds, then has it checked by a second operator.

error.defect_description: A switching step is missing or in the wrong order.

control.basis: Written and independently checked switching orders under the utility's work protection code

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Book the mobile substation and materials
steps.description: The supervisor confirms that parts and consumables are in stores, books one of the two mobile substations if customers cannot be carried by adjacent feeders, and confirms the crew and date with the control room.

evidence.note: Two mobile units per the organisation file; share of outages needing one is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up the mobile substation
steps.description: A crew tows the mobile substation to the station, levels and grounds it, connects primary and secondary cables, and tests it before the switching; it stays connected until the station equipment is back in service.

control.basis: Pre-energization tests and grounding of mobile equipment under the work protection code

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the mobile is held for the whole outage, two to seven days.

steps.name: Crew travels to the station
steps.description: The three-person crew loads tools, test sets and materials and drives to the station for the start of the outage window, usually early morning.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold the tailboard meeting
steps.description: The crew leader walks the crew through the job plan, isolation points, hazards, approach distances and emergency plan, and everyone signs the tailboard form.

control.basis: Pre-job hazard assessment and tailboard (Occupational Health and Safety Act duties; IHSA Electrical Utility Safety Rules)

evidence.note: Standard Ontario utility practice.

steps.name: Switch out and issue work protection
steps.description: The control room operator carries out the switching remotely through SCADA and with the crew at the station, confirms the equipment is isolated, and issues a work protection permit to the crew leader.

error.defect_description: Isolation point missed in the permit.

control.basis: Work protection issued only by the control room under the utility's work protection code

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Test for dead and apply grounds
steps.description: The crew tests each isolated conductor with a voltage detector, applies protective grounds and locks and tags the isolation points listed on the permit.

control.basis: Test before touch, grounding and lockout under IHSA Electrical Utility Safety Rules

evidence.note: Standard practice.

steps.name: Carry out the maintenance
steps.description: The crew performs the planned work: breaker timing and contact resistance tests and mechanism service, transformer power factor and turns ratio tests, tap changer inspection, battery impedance and discharge tests, switchgear cleaning and torque checks, and repairs found along the way.

error.defect_description: A test result is out of limits but recorded as acceptable, or a connection is left loose.

evidence.note: Test types from the source; durations and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Test protection and trip circuits
steps.description: The protection and control technologist injects test currents into the relays, checks trip and close circuits to the maintained breaker, and confirms settings match the protection database before the equipment goes back in service.

control.basis: Return-to-service testing of protection after maintenance (utility protection standard)

evidence.note: Relay testing after work from the source; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Remove grounds and restore
steps.description: The crew removes grounds and locks and surrenders the permit; the operator cancels the work protection, switches the equipment back in and the mobile substation is disconnected if one was used.

control.basis: Permit surrender before re-energizing under the work protection code

next.condition: defect found that needs parts not in stock

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Order parts and reschedule
steps.description: When the crew finds a failed bushing, tap changer part or breaker mechanism component that is not stocked, the supervisor raises a purchase requisition and puts the work order back on the outage plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for parts from the supplier
steps.description: The supplier quotes and delivers the part; station equipment parts are often made to order, so lead times run from weeks to several months.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of supplier lead time.

steps.name: Record results in the ERP
steps.description: The electrician types the readings, test results, defects found, materials used and hours into the ERP work order and timesheet, attaches the scanned sheet or test files, and raises a corrective work order for anything left open.

error.defect_description: Readings or test files missing, or hours charged to the wrong order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; paper sheets re-keyed in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review and close the work order
steps.description: The stations supervisor reads the completed order, compares readings with the previous visit, sends abnormal results to the asset management engineer and closes the order or returns it for missing information.

control.basis: Supervisor review of completed maintenance records (asset management records policy)

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Parts not in stock
exceptions.description: About 7% of outage jobs find a defect that needs a made-to-order part; the equipment is restored and the outage is replanned after the part arrives.

exceptions.name: Oil spill
exceptions.description: A leaking transformer or breaker is contained and reported to the environment team and possibly the province.

exceptions.name: Record returned
exceptions.description: The supervisor sends the work order back because readings or test files are missing.

evidence.note: The organisation file uses 91 from the 2020 annual report.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from work order release to close
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for a mix of about 75% monthly inspections and 25% outage maintenance

evidence.note: Monthly inspections are completed within the month and closed within a week; outage jobs are booked two to six weeks out. Not measured.

pain_points.description: Outage maintenance has to fit between summer and winter peaks and around two mobile substations, so jobs slip from season to season and the backlog grows on stations that are already past their expected life.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file reports about half of stations past expected life.

pain_points.description: Readings are written on paper or tablets and re-keyed into the ERP, so trends are hard to see and records come back for missing data.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Made-to-order station parts have long lead times, forcing a second outage.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: The not-so-secret life of power stations
sources.supports: 92 substations across the city in 2021; distribution substations step voltage down to under 10,000 volts; station transformers weigh up to 70,000 pounds and need a crane; stations use switchgear, fuses and breakers to isolate circuits.

sources.title: An Overview of Substation Maintenance: Its Evolution and Key Testing Practices (E. Khan)
sources.supports: Substation maintenance combines time-based, condition-based and performance-based strategies; transformer diagnostics include dissolved gas analysis, oil quality, power factor, winding resistance and turns ratio; breaker diagnostics include timing and motion and contact resistance; battery tests include impedance, voltage, specific gravity and discharge; relays are tested at commissioning and periodically.

sources.title: An in-depth look at Hydro Ottawa's grid maintenance
sources.supports: Routine inspections of transformers, switches and breakers follow a three-year cycle across the service territory; a critical pole program tests thousands of poles a year; maintenance holes are graded A to E; work often needs the area de-energized, which may need a planned outage; vegetation management units are on two- or three-year cycles; satellite imaging twice a year (introduced after the reference period).

assumptions: Monthly visits to every station and the quarterly or annual infrared and oil-sampling intervals are the organisation file's and the author's estimates; no opened source states the utility's station inspection interval. The 2024 Hydro Ottawa source gives a three-year cycle for routine inspection of transformers, switches and breakers across the territory, which may refer to distribution plant rather than stations.
The process map lists the trigger as the crew schedule from work scheduling; in practice the stations department plans its own preventive work in the ERP and the schedule only releases it.
Switching planners and control room operators take part in every outage job but are not in the process map's role list; they are included here at small FTE.
Outage work is shown with a three-person crew (people = 3); protection retesting runs alongside the end of the maintenance (concurrent_with).
The mobile substation is held for two to seven days per job that uses one; with about 10 such jobs a month and two units this keeps them busy for much of the spring and fall seasons.
Corrective work raised from findings (hot spots, DGA alerts) is a new work order and a new case, not a loop inside this one.
